Saudi Arabia has introduced a new employment regulation reserving 69 administrative support occupations in the private sector exclusively for Saudi nationals, effectively restricting foreign workers from occupying positions covered by the decision. As reported by MSN, Microsoft online news platform on Wednesday, the regulation, which took effect on October 4, 2026, requires private-sector employers to achieve a 100 per cent localisation rate across all 69 listed occupations. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development said: “The measure is designed to increase the participation of Saudi nationals in the labour market, create more employment opportunities for citizens and strengthen the country’s local workforce. “The affected occupations cover several administrative and support functions, including human resources management, recruitment, public relations, reception, translation, security and office administration. “Some of the positions include human resources managers, recruitment specialists, administrative assistants, receptionists, government relations clerks, secretaries, translators, data entry operators, warehouse keepers and security guards. Other affected professions include personnel managers, labour affairs managers, compensation specialists, career guidance specialists, protocol managers, talent managers and administrative investigation managers.” The ministry began enforcing the new regulation on October 4, deploying supervisory inspection teams across several regions to monitor private-sector establishments and assess their compliance with the localisation requirements. Businesses found violating the decision may face penalties under existing labour regulations. The ministry said the initiative forms part of Saudi Arabia’s broader labour market strategy, which seeks to increase employment opportunities for citizens, develop local skills and raise localisation levels across different economic sectors. The new requirement has implications for expatriates currently employed in the affected occupations, as private-sector employers are required to reserve the listed positions for Saudi nationals. Employers operating in the Kingdom are expected to review their staffing arrangements, identify affected positions and take necessary steps to comply with the 100 per cent localisation requirement. The development represents another step in Saudi Arabia’s ongoing efforts to expand employment opportunities for its citizens and increase their representation in the private sector.
